findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy: none; pct: 100

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud against customers and finance contacts; require DMARC enforcement plan pre-close and factor phishing risk into insurability review.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, monitoring rua reports and aligning SPF/DKIM senders.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier: ~all; lookup_count: 2

findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens anti-spoofing and compounds DMARC p=none; low-cost DNS fix should be a closing condition.

remediation.summary: Audit authorized senders, then change SPF ~all to -all in coordination with DMARC enforcement.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS increases spoofing/cache-poisoning risk for fleet portals; minor remediation, include in 100-day plan.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/registry, publish DS records, and monitor validation.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: CT names suggest VPN, legacy Jenkins, staging and legacy portal attack surface; diligence should confirm ownership, exposure and decommissioning before valuation of cyber risk.

remediation.summary: Inventory listed hosts, restrict or retire legacy/staging/admin systems, enforce MFA and patching on VPN.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests unmanaged sprawl; supports an asset-inventory condition in the value-creation plan.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to owners and business need; remove orphaned certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions: [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www may fail customer/ insurer security reviews and weaken transport security; quick config remediation.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, retain TLSv1.2+ with modern ciphers, and retest all hosts.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS allows downgrade to HTTP on first visit; minor, easily remediated gap for insurer questionnaires.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security header on apex and www, then consider preload after testing.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001; ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11; match_tier: appliance_exposed; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure to a KEV-listed SSL-VPN appliance (version not verified) could enable remote intrusion; urgent patch/version verification should be a pre-close diligence item.

remediation.summary: Verify ExampleGate version/patch against KEV CVE, patch or isolate appliance immediately if affected, and review VPN logs.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: date: 2025-08-14; Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified.; disclosed_within_months: 14; entity_match: exact

findings.deal_impact: Breach 14 months ago affecting ~3,100 individuals raises notification, litigation and insurability questions; request incident report, remediation proof and claims history.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident postmortem and regulator closure, verify remediation and monitoring, and confirm notification obligations completed.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: high for CC6.1-01: MFA not enforced for sampled administrative accounts with access to production.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: high for CC6.2-01: terminated users retained active access well beyond the 1-business-day requirement.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: high for CC7.2-01: SIEM alerts were not reviewed for a two-week period.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: medium for CC8.1-01: sampled production changes lacked documented peer approval.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 found 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 found 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting same-day automated revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 found alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and not reviewed for 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10-23, 2025).

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is p=none (policy: none), so the domain is not enforced and can be spoofed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: Public breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system with approx. 3,100 individuals notified.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone doesn't prove a host is live, but certificates for legacy-portal, jenkins-old, and staging-api have last_seen dates in 2026-07 to 2026-10, within the last 12 months, showing active maintenance contradicting decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual pen test control had no exceptions, but 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test, contradicting a clean result with no highs.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions: production data is backed up daily to immutable storage and restore tests are performed quarterly.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided and the report period ended 2026-03-31, but SOC 2 Section 5 states management plans to obtain a bridge letter covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request.

deal_recommendations.text: Make signing conditional on verification of the internet-facing appliance version and patch status, a compromise assessment of VPN logs, and a bring-down of security representations.

Commission a full diligence scope that independently reviews the known-exploited appliance exposure in Days 0–30 and validates management representations across the contradicted access, monitoring, and incident claims before signing, as required by the escalate decision [F-008] [C-001] [C-003] [C-005].

Seek a specific indemnity for pre-closing incident losses arising from the 2025-08-14 incident affecting approximately 3,100 individuals, with diligence and any remediation confirmation tracked through Days 31–60 under the escalate, full-diligence-before-signing decision [F-009].

Assume the known 2025-08-14 incident is likely excluded from representations and warranties coverage, obtain the incident and claims record in Days 31–60, and do not rely on that policy for pre-closing losses while the escalate decision remains in effect before signing [F-009].
Confirm insurability and likely cyber underwriting requirements before close, addressing unenforced email authentication and inconsistent administrative access controls scheduled for Days 31–60.

Impose a post-close covenant to complete remediation across access controls, alert review, change approval, email authentication, exposed legacy systems, transport security, incident follow-up, and the updated assurance letter, spanning Days 31–60 and Days 61–100, following the escalate decision and pre-signing diligence [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009] [F-014].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. Brightwater Fleet Systems, Inc. is rated D at 56.8 because a critical, potentially exploitable exposure is present [F-008], a publicly disclosed incident occurred within 24 months [F-009], and multiple management statements were contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-005]. Key risks: The internet-facing known-exploited appliance requires version verification [F-008]. The 2025-08-14 incident affected approximately 3,100 individuals [F-009]. Administrative multifactor authentication and timely removal of terminated-user access were inconsistent [F-010] [F-011]. Email spoofing is possible because authentication is not enforced, and alerts were unreviewed for two consecutive weeks [F-001] [F-012]. Management credibility: Of 9 statements, 7 were contradicted and 2 were supported, spanning access, offboarding, monitoring, email, incident history, legacy systems, and testing [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005] [C-006] [C-007]. Next steps: Complete Days 0–30 appliance verification and compromise assessment before signing [F-008]. Obtain the incident record and updated assurance documents before signing [F-009] [F-014].
key_questions_for_management: Provide the verified appliance version, patch status, and VPN log review for the known-exploited exposure [F-008].
Provide the incident postmortem, regulator closure, notification record, and claims history for the 2025-08-14 incident [F-009] [C-005].
Reconcile the statement that every administrative account is behind multifactor authentication with the sampled accounts that were not enforced [F-010] [C-001].
Reconcile the same-day offboarding statement with terminated users retaining access for 6, 11, and 19 business days [F-011] [C-002].
Provide evidence that security alerts are now reviewed and triaged daily following the two-week gap from Nov 10–23, 2025 [F-012] [C-003].
Confirm the plan and timetable to move email authentication from monitoring to enforcement and to strengthen sender policy [F-001] [F-002] [C-004].
Provide an inventory reconciling the 47 hostnames to owners and business need, including the status of legacy, staging, and administrative systems [F-004] [F-005] [C-006].
Provide the bridge letter through 2026-10-30 and the hosting provider report for the carved-out production infrastructure [F-014] [F-015].
